messages:
Tomas (customer): Hey team — started seeing structured-output parse failures after we switched to JSON mode with streaming. About 10% of responses throw a parse error in our consumer.
Maya (support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste a snippet of the raw stream you received? Also which model + SDK version?
Tomas (customer): Using redwood-text-2 (hosted) via node SDK v1.12. Request payload: `stream: true, mode: 'json'`. Here's the exact raw stream fragments we captured (copied from tcp dump):
```
{"items":[{"id":"a1","price":9.99,"meta":{"source":"v1"}}
{"items":[{"id":"a2","price":12.00}},{"id":"a3","price":7.5,"meta":{"source":"v1","extra":true}}]
```
Tomas (customer): Note the first object is missing the closing bracket between fragments (we see `} \n{"items":` directly) so our parser complains: unexpected token '{'
Maya (support): That looks like a streaming boundary split mid-array/object — could be chunked at a bad boundary. Do you always get this with the same prompt?
Tomas (customer): No, intermittent. Happens more under higher QPS and when responses are longer. We suspect ordering assumptions in our consumer + streaming chunking.
Li (sre): Can you share the request_id or trace-id from the SDK logs? I'll check ingress egress and LB chunking.
Tomas (customer): trace-id=trc_04f7b9. Attached full request+response logs in the ticket (linked).
Maya (support): Thanks — tagging @Priya from eng-ml for potential model-side buffering / newline encoding issues. Priya any ideas?
Priya (eng-ml): Quick read: two things to check — (1) streaming frames must be reassembled by the SDK/consumer; if the response generator emits two JSON tokens back-to-back without a streaming delimiter, naive line-based parsers break. (2) The extra `meta.extra` key isn't a big issue but schema drift combined with partial, split chunks can make partial objects look like extra keys when stitched wrongly.
Priya (eng-ml): Repro tip: run a high-concurrency run hitting the hosted endpoint with stream:true and capture raw tcp. If you see patterns like `...}"\n{"items":` it's a chunk boundary issue.
Maya (support): Can you try a quick repro with curl to confirm raw behavior? Example we asked Tomas to run: 
```
curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-text-2","input":"generate items list","stream":true,"mode":"json"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Tomas (customer): Ran it twice — first run clean, second run produced the split. Attached raw output.
Li (sre): On our side I see chunking at the proxy for the `trc_04f7b9` session: one 8KB chunk ending mid-object then next chunk begins with `{"items":`. Proxy isn't dropping bytes but the consumer needs to reassemble. Which SDK are you using to parse streamed JSON?
Tomas (customer): Node stream -> split by `\n` -> JSON.parse per line. We assumed each line is a full JSON object.
Maya (support): There is the mismatch — streaming mode does not guarantee one JSON object per line, only emits tokens as produced. Line-splitting parsers can break on long outputs. Recommend switching to a reassembly approach (buffer until valid JSON parsed) or use `mode: 'jsonl'` if you need per-line items.
Tomas (customer): Hmm we expected JSON mode to yield array items line-delimited. Could we get a server-side guard to never split inside array/object?
Priya (eng-ml): Not feasible at scale to guarantee chunk boundaries won't split tokens; chunking happens at transport. We can add clearer docs/examples showing reassembly patterns and provide an SDK helper to reassemble streaming JSON tokens.
Maya (support): Action items: (1) @Tomas, switch consumer to buffer-and-parse (or use jsonl) and confirm. (2) @Li, please correlate more sessions for 1 hour and escalate if chunk patterns indicate proxy misconfiguration. (3) @Priya, can we ship an SDK streaming helper and add a short KB article on safe JSON streaming parsing?
Tomas (customer): I can switch to buffer-based parsing and report back this afternoon. For now we flagged as P1 because it caused downstream pipeline crashes.
Li (sre): I've increased verbosity and will ping here with findings by +45m.
Priya (eng-ml): I'll prototype a small JS helper that collects chunks until parse succeeds and post a gist. Quick pseudo: 
```
let buf = '';
stream.on('data', (c) => { buf += c.toString();
  try { const obj = JSON.parse(buf); handle(obj); buf = ''; }
  catch(e) { /* wait for more */ }
});
```
Priya (eng-ml): Also will add note about schema drift: if arrays sometimes contain `meta.extra` we recommend consumers tolerate extra keys or validate presence of required keys (`id`, `price`) and skip partial items.
Maya (support): Thanks everyone. Tomas — marking the support ticket escalated to eng-ml and SRE. Please paste the curl raw output link in the ticket and update when you test the buffer approach. :thumbsup:
Tomas (customer): Will do, thanks.
deploy-bot: deploy redwood/proxy v2.14.1 succeeded (commit abc123)
Maya (support): Closing loop here after romping through logs — SRE says proxy chunking behavior within TCP is expected, and eng-ml will provide SDK helper and KB. Leaving this thread open until customer confirms workaround works.
